lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Look up on a clear day, and the sky is blue. But sunlight is white.

lines.speaker: C01
lines.text: So where does the blue come from?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tiny molecules in the air scatter short blue wavelengths much more than long red ones.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That scattered blue light reaches your eyes from every part of the sky. [pause 300ms] So the whole sky glows blue.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At sunset, light crosses much more air, so most of the blue is scattered away before it reaches you.

claims.text: Sunlight contains all visible wavelengths and appears white.
Air molecules scatter shorter (blue) wavelengths much more strongly than longer (red) ones, which makes the daytime sky blue.
At sunset sunlight travels through more atmosphere, so more blue is scattered out of the direct path and the sun and sky look orange-red.
